Hi Sergio / Laura,

Quick flag — NimbleOps (ISV partner) and Acero Analytics (integration partner) both have active pipeline / co-sell asks against a cluster of midwest accounts that we recently surfaced in PartnerOps. NimbleOps claims primary relationship on 8 accounts; Acero has active POC + two exec sponsors on 5 of those. This is starting to create duplicate outreach and confusion for the AE owners.

I've attached a mapping with the account rows annotated with ownership markers from partner intake forms and recent AE notes. Can we put together a short mediation call with both partners to land on who owns motion for each account (or agree to a joint co-sell play for specific accounts)?

Priority asks:
- Quick review of the attached overlap matrix (NimbleOps_Acero_overlap_matrix_20270711.xlsx)
- Tiebreaker rules we should apply (product fit, contract footprint, active exec sponsor, demo readiness)
- If we can't definitively split, propose a short canary co-sell approach with clear routing and crediting rules

I can coordinate partner invites once we align internally. Suggested window: next week (July 6–9) — daytime PT.

Thanks,
Stephanie

Thanks Steph — reviewed the matrix. A couple quick thoughts:

1) Tiebreaker order I usually apply:
   - Existing signed commercial relationship (billing/contract in place)
   - Executive sponsor with defined success criteria
   - Demo/POC already scheduled (time to value)
   - Strategic motion (ISV vs consultancy breadth)

2) For the contested cluster (accounts A-C), Acero has deeper technical build-out on record; NimbleOps shows closer commercial reach for accounts D-F.

3) Recommend we propose a 45-minute triage call with both partners + the AEs for the contested accounts and come out with a decision per-account. If we can't, we default to a short shared-co-sell pilot for 30 days with split credit (50/50) and an explicit routing rule.

I can lead the call from alliances side and will propose the above playbook as a starting point.

Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Alliances (Americas)

Agree with Sergio's framework. A couple additional constraints from GTM:

- We need to minimize AE context switching; wherever an AE already has an active close plan (opportunity stage >= proposal), we should default to the AE's preferred partner unless there's a documented escalation.
- For accounts where neither partner has a clear advantage, we should prioritize a pilot that accelerates pipeline (short POC + joint executive briefing).

I'm OK with the 45-minute mediation call. If partners push back on joint calls, we can do sequential interviews but that usually increases friction.

I'll carve out time July 7 at 10am PT as an initial slot. Steph — if you can invite, please include the AE owners and a short agenda (15 min pre-read + 30 min decision), and call out the expected crediting model if shared.
